fullPassage: There are deep similarities between viral contagion and behavioral contagion. For example, people in close or extended proximity to others infected by a virus are themselves more likely to become infected, just as people are more likely to drink excessively when they spend more time in the company of heavy drinkers. But there are also important differences between the two types of contagion. One is that visibility promotes behavioral contagion but inhibits the spread of infectious diseases. Solar panels that are visible from the street, for instance, are more likely to stimulate neighboring installations. In contrast, we try to avoid others who are visibly ill. Another important difference is that behavioral contagion can promote both desirable and undesirable behaviors, while disease contagion invariably spreads something harmful.

❌ ① 태양광 패널 자극 (일치): 'Solar panels that are visible ... are more likely to stimulate neighboring installations'와 같아요.

✅ ② 이로운 것과 해로운 것을 모두 ←정답: 본문은 'disease contagion invariably spreads something harmful(질병 전염은 언제나 해로운 것을 퍼뜨린다)'이라고 해요. '이로운 것도 퍼뜨린다'는 것은 행동 전염의 특징이라, 질병 전염에 대한 이 진술은 일치하지 않아요.

❌ ③ 과음 가능성 (일치): 'more likely to drink excessively when they spend more time in the company of heavy drinkers'와 같아요.

❌ ④ 바람직/바람직하지 않은 행동 모두 (일치): 'behavioral contagion can promote both desirable and undesirable behaviors'와 같아요.
det.tip: 질병 전염 = 언제나 harmful(해로운) 것만. 이로운 것 퍼뜨림은 행동 전염

ch: 거리에서 보이는 태양광 패널은 이웃의 설치를 자극할 가능성이 크다.

술을 많이 마시는 사람들과 더 많은 시간을 보내면 과음할 가능성이 커진다.
행동 전염은 바람직한 행동과 바람직하지 않은 행동을 모두 촉진할 수 있다.

questions.passage: There are deep similarities between viral contagion and behavioral contagion. For example, people in close or extended proximity to others infected by a virus are themselves more likely to become infected, just as people are more likely ①<u>to drink</u> excessively when they spend more time in the company of heavy drinkers. But there are also important differences between the two types of contagion. One is that visibility promotes behavioral contagion but ②<u>inhibits</u> the spread of infectious diseases. Solar panels that are visible from the street, for instance, are more likely to stimulate neighboring installations. In contrast, we try to avoid others ③<u>which</u> are visibly ill. Another important difference is that behavioral contagion can promote both desirable and undesirable behaviors, while disease contagion invariably ④<u>spreads</u> something harmful.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: which → who. 사람(others)을 받는 주격 관계대명사는 who예요.
det.analysis:
❌ ① to drink (○): 'more likely to drink'로 'be likely to do' 구조라 맞아요.

❌ ② inhibits (○): 단수 주어 visibility에 맞는 inhibits가 맞아요.

✅ ③ which → who ←정답: '______ are visibly ill'의 앞 명사는 사람(others)이에요. 사람을 받고 뒤에 동사(are)가 오는 주격 관계대명사는 who라서, 사물에 쓰는 which는 틀려요.

❌ ④ spreads (○): 단수 주어 disease contagion에 맞는 spreads가 맞아요.
det.tip: 사람 선행사(others) + 동사 → 주격 who (which는 사물용)

det.korean: visibly (눈에 띄게 — 부사)
det.analysis:
빈칸 뒤의 ill(아픈)은 형용사예요.

형용사를 앞에서 꾸며 주는 말은 부사이므로, 형용사 visible(눈에 보이는)을 부사 visibly(눈에 띄게)로 바꿔야 해요.

그래서 'visibly ill(눈에 띄게 아픈)'이 되어 정답은 visibly예요.
det.tip: 형용사 ill을 꾸미는 부사 → visible + -ly = visibly

[조건] (1) are, avoid, ill, others, to, try, visibly, we, who 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 9단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: 정답: we try to avoid others who are visibly ill (우리는 눈에 띄게 아픈 다른 사람들을 피하려고 한다)
det.analysis:
1) 주어+동사: '우리는 ~하려고 한다' → we try to. try to 뒤에는 동사원형이 와요.

2) 동사+목적어: '피하다' avoid + '다른 사람들' others → avoid others.

3) 꾸며 주는 절: '눈에 띄게 아픈'은 관계대명사 who로 이어요. 사람(others)을 받고 뒤에 동사가 오니 주격 who → who are visibly ill(눈에 띄게 아픈). 형용사 ill은 부사 visibly가 꾸며 줘요.

4) 합치면 we try to avoid others who are visibly ill, 9단어예요.
